Arbitrary correlated success indicators of orbit mean 1/p obey the exact raw complementary matched/unpaired-minus covariance identity. Dropping its nonnegative product-of-means subtraction gives product continuation plus a separately stopped joint-success loss.
Nonzero links preserve complete after-p masks, so every nonnegative kernel of the two preserved masks passes unchanged through both column capacities; a common outer probability is not squared.
Same-location projection is injective on assigned-row ancestor labels; removing later congruences does not duplicate a p-step matrix row, future-mask choice or column capacity.

In a growing equivalence-relation chronology, replacing endpoints by vertices connected to them earlier preserves their first-sharing epoch, preventing charges of one image pair at two different epochs.

An arbitrary finite sequence of nonnegative continuation factors and correlated one-step bounds is dominated by its terminal carried product and one separately stopped projected-transport charge per step, with no branching of stopped terms.

If P0=rho*H, d0<rho and both masks obey sum_{p|d,p>d0*B}(log p)^0.3/p<=1, then for fixed C>=0 the product of R_p^(-C) over p>P0 dividing UTde is at most exp(2*C*(1/(rho*log 2)+2/(log 2)^0.3)), independently of block and masks.
